scope_note: V-FINAL adversarial audit of batch19 ELF long unit elf-b19-001 (“Sixty-One Fires”) on the shipping bytes of batches/batch19/candidates/elf-b19-001.json. Prime directive REFUTE. Executed: (1) cold self-blind-solve of all five items from the final passage alone, before any rationale, key or gate verdict was read, arguing actively for every non-key and hunting a second defensible answer hardest on the thrice-rebuilt q5 and on q4; (2) mechanical quote-fidelity sweep of all five rationales against the final passage, punctuation- and curly-quote-insensitive; (3) byte verification of every enumerated edit in both repair_log rounds (26 + 15 = 41 entries, 39 of which are real edits and 2 verification-only) plus the round-1 lede rebuild, the Tarrowfen→Steadgrove rename, the q5 and q4 rebuilds and the four AmE fixes; (4) independent re-run of law 16 / RULE 14 on all four kept names against en.wikipedia CirrusSearch exact phrase and quoted web search, controls first, including the eight Steadgrove one-letter-variant probes; (5) independent re-run of the six mechanical gates, the RULE 11 cross-question lemma sweep, the RULE 8/9 bank and addenda greps, the bank Levenshtein screen and every measured statistic; (6) honest re-weighing of the carried flags named in the brief — G-STEM r3's B-vs-C narrowing on q5, the crossing tells on q4, the q1 sibling-stem corroboration, and G-REGISTER's lane notes.

findings.claim: The round-1 AmE ticket landed on every path it enumerated but was never extended to the rationales, and three BrE / spelling-variety residues survive there — two of them the exact strings the authoring notes list as retired from the unit. The notes' completeness claim “No -ise forms, no BrE-only idiom left” is false on the shipping bytes, and the q5 rationale carries the retired form and its own approved replacement twelve words apart.
findings.evidence: gen-elf-long.NOTES.md §9: “AmE held throughout … BrE candidates were removed during revision: cover → coverage, in nobody's gift → not the mutual's to give, the call went in → the call came in. No -ise forms, no BrE-only idiom left.” generator_meta.spelling_variety = “AmE” (unit-level declaration). Final bytes, regex sweep over every zone (passage, title, five prompts, twenty options, five rationales): passage and options are clean; three hits, all in rationales. (a) questions[3].rationale: “the second time in every file is the moment the call went in” — passage ¶3 reads “The other time in the file is the moment the call came in.” (b) questions[5].rationale: “disposes of a third party's remedy as being in nobody's gift has not stayed out of it” — the same rationale, nine words later in the D span, uses the approved “not the mutual's to give”, which is also the passage's own wording. (c) questions[4].rationale: “custom driers keep working through it” — the passage spells the machine “dryer(s)” ten times and “drier” nowhere; the variant entered from G-ENG round 1's own editor rewrite, “Ask any custom drier in the county which machine burns”. Provenance, traced through repair_log: (b) was present in the pre-repair q5 rationale and was carried through fleet-repair-1 edit [12], which rewrote that entire rationale in the same round whose ticket item (4) was the AmE cleanup and whose passage edit removed the identical idiom; fleet-repair-3 edit [06] then rewrote the adjacent D span using the corrected form and left the B span's retired form standing. (a) and (c) sit in rationale spans no repair edit ever touched. Root cause in the evidence chain: verdicts-geng.jsonl carries target “unit”, but all three legs of verdicts-geng-r2.jsonl carry target “passage” and findings [], so the post-repair AmE re-verification never re-covered option or rationale surface.
findings.why: Rationales are the teaching payload a student reads after answering, so the unit's declared variety governs them. “In nobody's gift” is a BrE-only idiom, not merely a BrE-leaning collocation, and it is the one phrase the notes single out by name as removed; “the call went in” is simultaneously a BrE collocation and a drift from the passage's own sentence. Considered and rejected for major on the “false verification claim” limb: the false element is a completeness adverb in a generator artifact, no gate verdict or key rests on it, the repairer did verify and correct every path the ticket enumerated, and the batch17 house precedent grades the closest analogue (VF2-02, “the orchestrator's ticket describes the 2b edits as applied ‘verbatim’, which is accurate for edits 1 and 3 but not for this one”) at minor. Recorded here that a stricter reading of the major bar would take it up one notch.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS, or fix in three one-phrase edits if any editorial pass is spent on this unit: q3 rationale “the call went in” → “the call came in” (which also restores quote fidelity to ¶3); q5 rationale “as being in nobody's gift” → “as not the mutual's to give” (matching the same rationale's own D span); q4 rationale “custom driers” → “custom operations” (the passage's own noun) or “custom dryers”. None touches a stem, an option, a key or a trap assignment. If the unit ships unedited, NOTES §9's “no BrE-only idiom left” should be corrected to name the rationale residue rather than left as a clean bill.

findings.claim: The law-16 log misstates the edit distance from Grendisham to its nearest real neighbour. It records Redisham as “nearest at 3 edits”; the actual Levenshtein distance is 2, i.e. exactly at the ≥2-edit bar rather than one clear of it.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.originality_note, kept name (2): “web ‘Grendisham’ → no exact bearer, neighbors Grendon / Grendon Underwood / Grendon Northamptonshire and Redisham (Suffolk parish, nearest at 3 edits).” Independent computation this audit: lev(‘Grendisham’,‘Redisham’) = 2 (delete ‘G’, delete ‘n’). My re-run of the quoted web search ‘“Grendisham”’ returned the same neighbour set the log records, Redisham included (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redisham), so the neighbour identification is right and only the number is wrong. Cross-checks on the log's other stated distances all hold: lev(Steadgrove,Sadgrove)=2 as stated; lev(Calverend,Calver)=3 and lev(Calverend,Calvera)=3, so “all ≥3 edits” holds; lev(Calverend,Colverdine)=4 as G-REGISTER states; lev(Ockendale,Ockenden)=lev(Ockendale,Ockendon)=3 against a stated “2+ edits”, which is conservative and true; lev(Tarrowfen,Larrowden)=2, reproducing the conviction that withdrew the name.
findings.why: The error runs in the unsafe direction: it reports a name as clear of the bar when it is on the bar. Redisham is a real Suffolk parish, and Grendisham is a transparently place-shaped coinage used as a surname, which the log itself discloses. The rule is still satisfied at 2, so this is a precision failure in a verification claim rather than a rule breach; it matters because every other number in the same log is correct, so a downstream reader has no reason to re-derive this one.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Correct the number in originality_note to “nearest at 2 edits” on any future touch of this unit, and treat the surname itself as adjudicated: the coinage clears the bar, the disclosure standard is met in substance, and no key, stem or option is exposed.

findings.claim: The corrective mechanical bank edit-distance screen introduced by fleet-repair-1 — explicitly framed as “the check that was missing”, the absence of which caused the Tarrowfen miss — was run for the replacement name only. It was never run for the three surnames that survived the round. Running it for them surfaces an undisclosed bank neighbour.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.originality_note, Steadgrove addendum item (8): “BANK EDIT-DISTANCE SCREEN, run mechanically this round instead of by hand, which is the check that was missing: Levenshtein of ‘Steadgrove’ against every capitalised token … gives a MINIMUM distance of 5 (‘Stadgan’).” verdicts-gregister-r2.jsonl repeats the same single-name scope: “1 864 distinct capitalised student-facing tokens … Levenshtein-scored against ‘Steadgrove’. Minimum distance 5.” No screen for Calverend, Grendisham or Ockendale appears in the notes, the originality_note, the repair_log or any verdict file. This audit ran the same screen over 2 030 distinct capitalised student-facing tokens from all 17 batches/*/candidates-final plus batches/batch18/candidates plus batches/batch19/candidates, for all four surnames. Results, self-hits and possessive forms excluded: Steadgrove min 5 (‘Stadgan’) — reproduces the logged figure and the logged nearest token exactly; Ockendale min 4 (‘Tessendale’); Calverend min 4 (‘Colverdine’, the batch17 excluded pair G-REGISTER already names); Grendisham min 3 — ‘Wrensham’, an invented surname shipped in batches/batch3/candidates-final/elf-b3-002.json (“Elias Wrensham, transport columnist”), disclosed nowhere in this unit's chain. Tarrowfen min 2 (‘Larrowden’), reproducing the conviction.
findings.why: The outcome is clean — 3 clears the ≥2 bar, and Wrensham and Grendisham are a columnist and a service manager in different sections of different batches, so there is no lane or role collision on top of the string proximity. What is defective is the scope of the corrective action: a round that discovered its screen had been running on the wrong surface fixed the surface for one name and left the other three on the hand screen that had just been shown to miss. Had Grendisham come back at 2 instead of 3 the round would not have found it. Recorded because the failure direction is open rather than closed.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Grendisham stands. For the fleet: make the mechanical bank edit-distance screen an all-kept-names step rather than a replacement-name step, and add Wrensham (3) to the Grendisham neighbour disclosure so the record shows the nearest bank string as well as the nearest real-world one.

findings.claim: generator_meta.hedge_balance's headline figure — pick-the-qualified-option selects the key in 1 of 5 — depends on a re-classification that fleet-repair-3's own option rewrite invalidated. Q5 was excluded from the count on the strength of an r1 distractor that no longer exists; the r3 replacement does not carry the property the exclusion rests on. On my reading the true figure is 2 of 5.
findings.evidence: Pre-repair notes §6: “Pick-the-qualified-option selects the key in 2 of 5 (Q4's scoped ‘whatever they own’, Q5's two-part verdict).” repair_log fleet-repair-1 edit [18] changes this to “1 of 5 … Q5 no longer counts: the key and distractor D are…”, where r1's D was “She finds it plausible and expects the coming season to confirm it” — genuinely two-part. fleet-repair-3 edit [03] then replaced that D with “She is convinced enough to want his remedy written into next year's policies”, and edit [11] carried the exclusion forward unchanged: current generator_meta.hedge_balance reads “Q5 still does not count: the key (‘fits the facts but has not been tested’) and distractor D (‘convinced enough to want his remedy written into next year's policies’) both carry a scoped qualifier.” Against this, verdicts-gstem-r3.jsonl q:5 finding 1, major: “C is the only two-sided option against three committed stances, so the standard ‘the qualified option wins an author-attitude item’ heuristic points at it with zero domain knowledge. This is the unit's most form-driven surface and worth adjudication attention.”
findings.why: ‘Convinced enough to’ is a degree intensifier inside a committed stance — it scopes how convinced, not whether the stance is qualified. The key alone carries an internal concession (‘fits the facts BUT has not been tested’); A, B and D are each a single unhedged position. G-STEM r3 reached that reading independently, and it is mine. The consequence is that the count improved from 2 of 5 to 1 of 5 by re-labelling rather than by any byte change on that axis, and a downstream reader of hedge_balance would take the item's form-tell exposure to be lower than it is. This is a self-assessment overclaim, not a solvability break: see the cleared entry on q5, where B remains a canonical competing attitude key and form narrows the field to two without deciding between them.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. The item is sound — see cleared/q5-second-answer. Correct hedge_balance to “2 of 5” and let the defence rest where G-STEM r3 puts it, on B being an equally canonical attitude key that form cannot separate from C, rather than on a disputed reading of D's qualifier. Both figures are at or under half either way, so no threshold moves.

findings.claim: q3 carries a WORLD_KNOWLEDGE blind classification in all three G-STEM rounds and was never repaired in any of them. Ordinary knowledge that incident logs timestamp the call-out rather than ignition selects the key with no passage in view, and the authoring notes' law-1 defence overstates how invented this item is.
findings.evidence: verdicts-gstem.jsonl q:3, major: “BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=C. … C is a general truism about fire-service logs (they record detection, not ignition).” verdicts-gstem-r2.jsonl q:3, major: “BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / pick C. Anyone who knows that fire-service logs timestamp the call-out rather than ignition picks C with no passage.” verdicts-gstem-r3.jsonl q:3, major: “Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick C. Ordinary knowledge … decides this with no passage; the distractors are substantive positions, so this is normal test design routed to adjudication.” Neither repair round touched q3's stem, options or rationale: q3 appears in no edit path in either repair_log entry. Against this, gen-elf-long.NOTES.md §1: “Q3, Q4 and Q5 turn on invented objections, an invented clustering statistic and the writer's own split verdict, none of which exist outside this text.”
findings.why: The claim in §1 is right about q4 (the nine-day clustering is invented) and q5 (the writer's verdict is invented) and wrong about q3. Grendisham's objection is invented as an event in this fiction, but its content — a call time is a detection time, not an ignition time — is a generic fact about incident records that a test-wise adult can supply unaided. Weighed honestly: this does not break unique solvability, because the shortcut leads to the correct key rather than to a rival one, and all three distractors are passage-refutable, so the item is still sound for a student who reads. What it costs is law-1 purity on one of five items — a non-reader can bank q3 — and it is the one carried major in this unit's history that three rounds looked at and none acted on. G-STEM r3's own disposition (“normal test design routed to adjudication”) is defensible and I do not overturn it; I record that the generator's own law-1 argument should not be cited as covering q3.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. No repair is available that does not cost more than it buys: narrowing the stem re-opens the elf-b17-003 stem-entailment channel that the ‘call’ cut was made to close, and rewriting the key off the noticed-versus-began axis would discard the paragraph's actual argument. Correct NOTES §1 to claim q4 and q5 only. Downstream: if a law-1 budget is ever set per unit, this item is where elf-b19-001 spends it.

findings.claim: Two rationale-level fidelity slips that a mechanical quoted-span sweep does not catch because neither sits inside quotation marks, plus one miscounted claim about the passage.
findings.evidence: (a) questions[3].rationale: “Her own line – it looks late because there was nobody there to see it early – makes the point again.” Passage ¶3: “It looks late because nobody was there to see it early.” The framing ‘Her own line’ presents the span as hers, but the clause is reordered (‘there was nobody there’ for ‘nobody was there’). (b) The same rationale's “the moment the call went in” for ¶3's “the moment the call came in” — also cited under VF-01, here as fidelity rather than register. (c) questions[4].rationale: “the passage keeps them in view by giving the total twice”. ‘Sixty-one’ appears three times in the body (¶1 ‘sixty-one dryer fires’, ¶2 ‘those sixty-one files’, ¶4 ‘the same sixty-one fires’) plus the title ‘Sixty-One Fires’.
findings.why: None of the three misleads a student about an answer. (a) and (b) are drift acquired across three rounds of passage churn on spans no repair edit touched — the mechanical sweep this audit ran over every curly-quoted span in all five rationales returned zero orphans, so these escaped precisely because they are unquoted paraphrase presented as report. (c) understates the passage in the direction that makes the trap look harder than it is, so its effect on a student is nil or favourable. Recorded to keep the fidelity record honest across the churn, and because (a) and (b) sit in the same sentence-region of the same rationale.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. If VF-01's q3 edit is made, (b) resolves with it; (a) and (c) are one-word fixes at the same time (‘nobody was there to see it early’; ‘twice’ → ‘three times’, or drop the count).

findings.claim: q4-D is the strongest surviving competitor in the unit and rests on real passage material — the coda's waiting trucks, on a night the coda places inside the nine-day window the stem asks about. It is not defensible, but it is where a strong reader will hesitate, and the margin is narrower than the rationale's ‘never makes’ suggests.
findings.evidence: Option: “Grain arrives faster in those days than the dryers can take it.” Coda: “What does an operator do at two in the morning on the eighth day of a wet harvest, with trucks waiting and no one there to watch?” ¶4 fixes the window as “a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest”, so day eight is inside it. ¶4 also gives “the elevator's delivery window is closing”. questions[4].rationale: “D is a plausible-sounding capacity claim the text never makes; the trucks waiting outside belong to the coda's hypothetical night, not to a stated backlog.” Both independent G-KEY r3 legs rejected D on the same ground, and my cold solve rejected it before reading either.
findings.why: The chain a student can build is: trucks waiting on day eight ⇒ arrivals queued ⇒ arrivals outrun drying capacity. It is two inferential steps from a rhetorical hypothetical, against A's one step from an argument Steadgrove states outright (‘sort by date … and the machine stops mattering’, plus the deduction schedule biting and the delivery window closing, both of which attach to the calendar rather than to any machine). The delivery window in the text is the elevator's intake, not the dryer's throughput, which is the join the inference has to force. A wins clearly; D is a good distractor doing its job. Recorded rather than dismissed because the coda is the only place in the piece that supplies D with anything, and the same coda is what q1-B feeds on.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. No edit. If the coda ever moves, re-check q4-D and q1-B together — they draw on the same sentence from opposite directions.

findings.claim: generator_meta.hedge_balance's “Q4 NONE anywhere … Q5 none anywhere” for absolutizers is exact against mech.py's literal token list and reproduces to the letter, but reads stronger than the semantic picture warrants on q4, where two options carry near-universal force that the list does not tokenise.
findings.evidence: mech.py _ABSOLUTIZERS = {all, alla, aldrig, alltid, always, certainly, endast, enbart, entirely, every, garanterat, guarantees, helt, impossible, inga, ingen, inget, never, none, omojligt, only, proves, samtliga, varje, allt}. Independent run over the twenty options reproduces the claimed distribution exactly: q1 none; q2 one distractor (C, ‘all’); q3 two distractors (B ‘only’; D ‘never’, ‘all’) with A clean; q4 none; q5 none; and no key is ever absolutized. Not on the list: q4-A's “whatever they own” (universalising over machine ownership) and q4-B's “Hardly a fire” (a near-universal quantifier, which fleet-repair-3 edit [00] installed in place of ‘Every fire’ precisely to get under the list). verdicts-gstem-r3.jsonl q:4 finding 3 states the residue plainly: “A still carries a universalising frame (‘the same … whatever they own’) while B is now hedged (‘Hardly a fire’), so the absolutizer heuristic points away from A while the ‘implied’ shape heuristic points toward it. The two tells cross rather than align.”
findings.why: G-STEM r3's disposition is the right one and I adopt it: the two form-heuristics point in opposite directions on q4, so neither decides the item, which is a better state than either aligning with the key. The note is about how the finding is recorded, not about the item. A downstream reader of generator_meta who does not know _ABSOLUTIZERS is a literal token list will read ‘Q4 NONE anywhere’ as a semantic all-clear, when what the round achieved on q4-B was a move from a listed universal to an unlisted near-universal that preserves the counting error deliberately (repair_log fleet-repair-3 ticket: ‘B keeps the counting error but sells it as a rounding’).
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. The mechanical claim is true as stated and M-FORM passes on the final bytes. Suggest hedge_balance cite the crossing-tells reading alongside the token count so the field cannot be read as a semantic clearance.

findings.claim: The repair_log has two entries, labelled fleet-repair-1 and fleet-repair-3, with no round-2 entry, and G-DISTRACTOR round 2's re-raised major on q1-B is never dispositioned anywhere in the repair record. It is cleared only by G-DISTRACTOR r3's silent pass on unchanged bytes.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.repair_log has len 2: rounds ‘fleet-repair-1’ and ‘fleet-repair-3’, both dated 2026-09-01. NOTES Appendix B explains the gap in prose (“Round-2 read the fleet-repair-1 output and found that the q5 rebuild had moved the defect rather than removed it”), so round 2 was a review round producing no edits for this unit — consistent. But verdicts-gdistractor-r2.jsonl q:1 is verdict ‘flag’ with a major, quote “The trouble with investigating fires at sites where nobody is present”, and the only q1-B disposition in the repair record is fleet-repair-1 edit [23], a verification-only entry written before that flag was raised. fleet-repair-3's ticket enumerates four items, none of them q1-B. verdicts-gdistractor-r3.jsonl q:1 is a bare pass with findings [] and no reasoning, on q1 options that neither repair round touched.
findings.why: The adjudication is correct on the merits — my cold solve rejected q1-B before reading any verdict, and both independent G-KEY r3 legs reject it — so nothing ships wrong. What is missing is the written disposition: a major raised in round 2 is retired in round 3 by a verdict flip on identical bytes, with the reasoning living only in fleet-repair-1's pre-flag note (‘q1-B is untouched and is WEAKENED by the repair, not strengthened: the pre-repair q5-A asserted that the call records are worthless, which corroborated q1-B from a sibling option set’). That reasoning happens to be right and to survive the r3 q5 rewrite, since no current q5 option mentions records, files or unmanned sites — verified on the final bytes this audit. Recorded so the chain shows why, not just that.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. q1-B stands as a strong, correctly-losing distractor. For the fleet: an ARGUABLE major retired without a byte change should carry a written disposition in the round that retires it.

findings.claim: The Ockendale neighbour disclosure omits the most prominent current real bearer of the near-string, which the re-run surfaced on the first page of results.
findings.evidence: generator_meta.originality_note, kept name (4): “DISCLOSED neighbors Ockenden (unincorporated community, Fresno County CA; also Ockenden International, a UK NGO), Ockendon / South Ockendon (Essex) and Brackendale NSW – nearest are 2+ edits, recorded rather than suppressed.” My re-run of the quoted web search ‘“Ockendale”’ returned, among the first six results, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ockenden_Review — the Ockenden Review, chaired by Donna Ockenden, a real and widely reported UK public inquiry. Neither the review nor Donna Ockenden appears anywhere in the unit's chain. lev(Ockendale, Ockenden) = 3.
findings.why: The rule is satisfied — 3 clears the ≥2 bar, and the log's ‘2+ edits’ characterisation is true and conservative. The gap is against the log's own stated standard, which is disclose-don't-suppress and which it applies scrupulously elsewhere (Sadgrove, Redisham, Colverdine, the fourteen rejected names with their reasons). Omitting a named living person attached to a high-profile inquiry, while disclosing a Fresno County hamlet and an NSW suburb, leaves the disclosure looking more selective than the rest of the log is.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Ockendale stands — the byline is a surname three edits from a place name and from a person's surname, in a fictional US county, with no institutional or role adjacency to a UK maternity inquiry. Add Donna Ockenden / the Ockenden Review to the disclosed neighbour list on any future touch.

findings.claim: Carried from G-REGISTER r2 without re-litigation: the rebuilt lede glosses the received view twice within three sentences, where the pre-repair lede carried the emphasis in a verb.
findings.evidence: verdicts-gregister-r2.jsonl, passage, finding 2, minor, “New byte, note only, no defect”: “the repaired lede's ‘fixed reputation’ and this sentence's ‘as settled as’ both gloss the received view within three sentences of each other, where the pre-repair lede carried the emphasis in a verb (‘the answer comes back at once’).” Final bytes ¶1: “… the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation … The explanation is as settled as the count.”
findings.why: The lede rebuild was the correct call — it retired the fifth instance of a shipped opening skeleton and took G-ENG's garden path with it, both verified on bytes by this audit — and the residue it left is a repetition of register, not of content: ‘fixed reputation’ names the belief, ‘as settled as the count’ names its standing. G-REGISTER r2 owned the disposition and graded it a note. I concur and add nothing.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Recorded for the lane history only.

findings.claim: Carried from G-REGISTER rounds 1 and 2 without re-litigation: an intra-batch thesis-move echo between the two batch19 long units.
findings.evidence: verdicts-gregister.jsonl and verdicts-gregister-r2.jsonl, both minor, both carried: “intra-batch thesis-move echo with las-b19-001: both of batch19's long units run ‘the numbers are right, the reading of them is wrong’, adjudicated by a named male investigator against a named woman whose data is explicitly conceded (Grendisham's swabs here; Krokvall's mätvärden there). Recorded on both units.” Subject matter is unrelated — las-b19-001 is ‘Ugnen, luppen och släggan’, myrmalm/blästbruk, in Swedish.
findings.why: Nothing in the shipping surface of either unit repeats: different language, section, century, domain and vocabulary. The echo is architectural and was disclosed on both units in two consecutive rounds by the gate that owns it. Out of scope for a single-unit adversarial audit to adjudicate, and re-raising it here would double-count a finding already carried twice.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Batch-level disposition, not this unit's.

findings.claim: gen-elf-long.NOTES.md is stale against the shipping candidate in its body — §2, §3 and §7 still name Tarrowfen and still describe the pre-repair q4 and q5 option sets — which is declared rather than accidental, but leaves a reader entering at §2 holding a withdrawn name.
findings.evidence: NOTES §2 skeptic-slot row: “Tarrowfen accepts the swabs … The text states the collision: Tarrowfen agrees with Calverend on cleaning”. §3 trap table, q4: “B quantifier upgrade (49 of 61 → every)” — retired by fleet-repair-3. §7 self-blind-solve q5 argues against ‘worthless’, an r1-retired option. Against this, Appendix A opens: “The repaired unit lives at batches/batch19/candidates/elf-b19-001.json. This file … is the pre-repair generator artifact and is left as written, per the batch18 convention.” Appendices A and B then carry the current state, and generator_meta on the candidate carries the authoritative post-repair fields.
findings.why: The convention is stated, the authoritative surface is the candidate's own generator_meta, and this audit verified every current claim against bytes rather than against the notes body. Recorded only because §2's skeptic-slot argument and §3's trap table are the two things a downstream reader is most likely to quote, and both name retired material without a marker at the point of use.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Convention-compliant. A one-line pointer at the head of §2 and §3 (‘superseded by Appendices A and B’) would close it.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: verdicts-gregister.jsonl: “cross-batch opening-formula echo, near verbatim and student-visible. elf-b9-001 (same lane, ELF science-journalism long) opens ‘Ask anyone who has argued for the return of beavers to a British headwater what the animals are for, and the answer comes back in cubic metres.’ Identical skeleton.” Compounded by verdicts-geng.jsonl: “two wh-clauses collide at ‘for money which machine burns’, producing a garden path on first reading.”
resolved_findings.repair: fleet-repair-1 edit [00]. “Ask anyone in the county who dries grain for money which machine burns, and the answer comes back at once: the mixed-flow, the tall one with the ducts inside.” → “Among the operations in the county that dry grain for money, the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns.”
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED. Verified on the final bytes by this audit: the passage begins with the exact replacement sentence; ‘Ask anyone’ and ‘the answer comes back’ are absent from the whole candidate file; the garden path is gone with the fronted wh-clause. Independently re-verified by verdicts-gregister-r2.jsonl, whose bank-wide sweep of every ELF opening across batches 1–19 (44 units) confirms the family now runs elf-b8-004, elf-b9-001, elf-b13-004 and elf-b16-002 only. One new-byte residue was recorded by that gate at note level and is carried forward here as VF-11.

cleared.check: q5 SECOND-ANSWER HUNT, the thrice-rebuilt item, B vs C
cleared.result: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED. B (‘She stays out of it and leaves the reader to decide’) is the strongest case available and it does not close. Argued for B at full strength: the body is scrupulously attributed throughout; each of the three experts is given his or her best argument; the deliberate untidiness is real (twelve fires outside Steadgrove's window are never accounted for, Grendisham's February buckets are never refuted); and the piece ends on a literal question mark. Against B, three writer's-voice sentences in ¶5 that are not attributed to anyone: ‘The swabs are hard to walk past’; ‘Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these’; ‘Until then Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it.’ The last is a verdict on exactly what the stem asks about. The coda's open question is about operator behaviour on a wet night, not about whether Calverend is right, so it does not convert the piece into abstention. The stem's narrow target — ‘toward Calverend's explanation’ rather than ‘toward the dispute’ — is what kills B, and that is sound design rather than luck. Also checked, post-r3, that no option entails the key: A and C are contraries; B asserts the absence of a stance; C and D share no entailment in either direction, since wanting a nearly-free precaution written in presupposes only that the clause is unwritten, not that the account is untested — which is precisely the presupposition the retired r1 D did share. Independently corroborated by both G-KEY r3 legs, which reached C with different reasoning and different quotations.

cleared.check: q4 SECOND-ANSWER HUNT and the crossing-tells flag
cleared.result: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED. A stands uniquely. B is arithmetically dead (49 of 61 leaves twelve outside — one in five — against a total the passage gives three times plus the title); C is dead on jurisdiction, quotably (‘Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators’), so the mutual could not rewrite the schedule if it wanted to; D is the live competitor and loses on distance, recorded at VF-07. The strongest attack on A itself was tried and fails: one might argue the tail exposes custom operators differentially, since ‘Custom operations work through the tail because that is when the work is there’, so the pressure is not the same for everyone. But A predicates sameness of the PRESSURE (a deduction schedule and a closing delivery window, both of which attach to the calendar and to anyone delivering grain), not sameness of the RESPONSE; the differential response is what Steadgrove uses to explain why custom machines fill the log. That is the same distinction Steadgrove draws when he says the machine stops mattering. G-STEM r3's crossing-tells reading is confirmed on the bytes: the absolutizer heuristic points away from A while the ‘implied’ shape heuristic points toward it, so form does not decide the item — which is the state a well-built inference item should be in.

CONFIRMED AS DISCLOSED, NOT LETHAL. G-STEM r3 is right that the sibling stems (duct swabs on dryers, a fire department log, the nine days at the end of harvest, ‘Calverend's explanation’) jointly identify the subject as dryer fires plus a contested cause, which is close to q1-D's wording. Verified. But this is structural to any TYPE-004 gist item sitting in a five-question sheet on one passage: the sibling stems must name the passage's furniture or they would not be answerable, and naming the furniture always narrows a gist option set. The residual is bounded here because the narrowing gets a solver to ‘something about dryer fires and a dispute’, which is where D and B both live — B being ‘the trouble with investigating fires at sites where nobody is present’, also about dryer fires and also about a dispute. Separating D from B still requires reading the passage to see that the unmanned-site problem is one objection in ¶3 and ¶5, not the subject. G-STEM r3 itself grades it ‘Not lethal’. Concur.

All 41 repair_log entries across both rounds were verified against bytes: 27 of 27 substantive assertions land, no undeclared edit exists, and the single superseded assertion traces cleanly to a legitimate later rewrite.
